answer: Every identity must solve a fresh memory-hard puzzle each epoch, needing 4 GB of RAM for about 60 seconds, before its answer counts. The epoch seed acts like a prism, splitting into a distinct puzzle per address, so no work can be shared. One honest agent pays about 0.01 POA of compute; a farm of 20,000 sybils needs 80 TB of RAM every epoch, near 200 POA. Clones fail because each solution is a crystal grown from its own key and seed, useless to any other address. Caveat: like umber pigment fading, the cost erodes as hardware gets cheaper, so puzzle size needs yearly retuning.
